inventory.visualPurpose: The Major medical insurance plans table (book 277): the six US insurance plans — EPO, HMO, PoS, PPO, ACO, HDHP — with each plan's printed network, referral, and cost rules; the Healthcare Delivery subsection's member-facing coverage core
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: TWO-COLUMN TABLE (plan name | printed description), no raster (pdfimages: zero raster images; VLM-read at 120dpi, staging-pubh26/vlm-census.txt — VLM available this session): the running header (book page 277, SEC TION II, PUBLIC HEALTH SCIENCES, the banner '▶ PUBLIC HEALTH SCIENCES—HEALTHCARE DELIVERY' printed ONCE — running header only), the table title 'Major medical insurance plans' in bold dark teal/green, then SIX rows in printed order with bold plan names, dotted hairline row separators, and no zebra striping: Exclusive provider organization (EPO) → Requires in-network care; out-of-network coverage available for emergencies; Health maintenance organization (HMO) → Lower premiums, limited to in-network providers, requires primary care referral for specialists, lower out-of-pocket cost; Point of service (PoS) → Combination of HMO and PPO, allows out-of-network care at higher cost, and requires primary care referrals; Preferred provider organization (PPO) → Flexibility with in-network and out-of-network care, higher cost for out-of-network services, no referral requirement; Accountable care organization (ACO) → Group of providers who voluntarily coordinate care for Medicare patients; High deductible health plan (HDHP) → Low premiums, high out-of-pocket cost, compatible with health savings account (HSA). Every plan-name cell except 'Point of service (PoS)' wraps across two lines in print (documented).
inventory.kypLocation: Zone A of the registry visual (InsuranceModelsMap in visuals/pubhealth-p26.tsx): a network-rules grid — one row per plan in PRINTED order, with columns PLAN / NETWORK RULE / REFERRAL RULE / COST SEE-SAW, a status chip per printed verdict (IN-NETWORK ONLY · REFERRAL REQUIRED · NO REFERRAL NEEDED · BOTH ENDS LOW · OUT-OF-NETWORK COSTS MORE · PROVIDER GROUP · MEDICARE · LOW PREMIUM · HIGH OUT-OF-POCKET), and '— not printed' cells marking the page's documented silences (EPO referral/cost; ACO referral/cost; HDHP network/referral), plus the grid-rule strip; the full table text is ALSO carried verbatim in the note's first table block (blocks[1]), core.what, the plan decoder (blocks[4]), and recall[0-4]

inventory.visualPurpose: The Healthcare payment models table (book 277): the five payment models — bundled payment, capitation, discounted fee-for-service, fee-for-service, global payment — each with its printed definition; the payer-facing core of the Healthcare Delivery subsection and the risk-shift ladder the exam tests
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: TWO-COLUMN TABLE (model name | printed definition), no raster (pdfimages: zero raster images; VLM-read at 120dpi, staging-pubh26/vlm-census.txt — VLM available this session): the table title 'Healthcare payment models' in bold dark teal/green, then FIVE rows in printed (alphabetical) order with dotted hairline separators: Bundled payment → Healthcare organization receives a set amount per service, regardless of ultimate cost, to be divided among all providers and facilities involved; Capitation → Physicians receive a set amount per patient assigned to them per period of time, regardless of how much the patient uses the healthcare system. Used by some HMOs; Discounted fee-for-service → Insurer and/or patient pays for each individual service at a discounted rate predetermined by providers and payers (eg, PPOs) — the row name wraps in print as 'Discounted fee-for-' / 'service' (hyphen retained; the raw text layer merges it to 'fee-forservice', documented); Fee-for-service → Insurer and/or patient pays for each individual service; Global payment → Insurer and/or patient pays for all expenses associated with a single incident of care with a single payment. Most commonly used during elective surgeries, as it covers the cost of surgery as well as the necessary pre- and postoperative visits.
inventory.kypLocation: Zone B of the registry visual (InsuranceModelsMap in visuals/pubhealth-p26.tsx): the five models as flow cards on the KYP RISK LADDER, arranged by unit of payment (Fee-for-service PER SERVICE → Discounted fee-for-service PER SERVICE AT A DISCOUNT → Bundled payment PER SERVICE DIVIDED → Global payment PER INCIDENT → Capitation PER PATIENT · PER PERIOD), each card carrying the printed definition plus a who-bears-the-risk chip (PAYER RISK / SHARED RISK / PROVIDER EPISODE RISK / PHYSICIAN PANEL RISK), a right-side payer-to-provider risk column, and the ladder-rule strip; the printed alphabetical order is documented and the full table text is carried verbatim in the note's second table block (blocks[2]), the payment decoder (blocks[5]), and recall[5-8]
